papers.title: Antimicrobial Sol–Gel Glassy Surfaces for Modification of Dental Implant Abutments to Reduce Microbial Adhesion
papers.abstract: Microbial colonization is a major factor contributing to peri-implantitis, and creating durable glassy surfaces with antimicrobial agents such as silver and copper may reduce microbial accumulation on dental abutments. This study aimed to develop antimicrobial thin-film glassy surfaces on Ti6Al4V alloy and to evaluate their surface and mechanical properties, antimicrobial effectiveness, and biocompatibility before and after thermal aging. A sol–gel-derived glassy matrix (G) was synthesized, and two antimicrobial coatings were prepared by incorporating ionic Ag (GAg) or a combination of Ag/Cu (GAgCu). Ti6Al4V specimens; these were either left uncoated or dip-coated with G, GAg, or GAgCu and cured at 450 °C. Half of the specimens underwent thermal aging between 5 °C and 55 °C for 3000 cycles. Surface roughness, contact angle, hardness, adhesion strength, scratch resistance, cytotoxicity (Agar diffusion and MTT assay on L929 fibroblasts), and microbial adhesion were evaluated using Streptococcus sanguinis, Porphyromonas gingivalis, and Candida albicans as representative oral microorganisms. Both coatings exhibited low surface roughness, hydrophilic surfaces, improved hardness, and significantly reduced microbial adhesion for all tested species. GAg showed superior mechanical properties, whereas GAgCu demonstrated a relatively stronger antimicrobial effect. Cytotoxicity tests indicated that all coatings were biocompatible at levels suitable for oral use. Overall, these coatings demonstrated strong adhesion, durability, and antimicrobial activity, suggesting their suitability for dental abutments made of Ti6Al4V.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少牙科基台上微生物定植，预防种植体周围炎。
summary_zh.method: 在Ti6Al4V上制备含银/铜的溶胶-凝胶玻璃涂层，进行热老化后评估性能。
summary_zh.result: 涂层具有低粗糙度、亲水性、改善硬度，并显著减少微生物粘附。
summary_zh.validation: 通过硬度、附着力、刮擦测试及细胞毒性实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To reduce microbial colonization on dental abutments and prevent peri-implantitis by developing durable antimicrobial glassy coatings.
summary_en.method: Sol-gel derived glassy coatings with ionic Ag or Ag/Cu were dip-coated on Ti6Al4V specimens, cured at 450°C, and half were thermally aged before characterization.
summary_en.result: Coatings exhibited low roughness, hydrophilicity, improved hardness, and significantly reduced adhesion of oral microorganisms.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties (hardness, adhesion, scratch resistance) and biocompatibility (cytotoxicity assays) were experimentally evaluated.

papers.title: Effect of Laser Surface Melting on the Microstructure and Corrosion Resistance of Laser Powder Bed Fusion and Wrought Ti-6Al-4V Alloys
papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-4V, a popular biomedical alloy, is increasingly fabricated by additive manufacturing methods, like laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). However, rapid thermal cycling and steep temperature gradients often induce mechanical degradation, corrosion, and wear. To address these challenges, laser surface modification is explored. This study investigates the microstructure and corrosion behaviour (simulated body fluid, 37 °C) of LPBF and wrought Ti-6Al-4V after laser surface melting (LSM) treatment. LSM produced modified layers of 1250–1350 µm (LPBF) and 1530–1600 µm (wrought), with gradients from remelted dendrites to acicular martensite. Microhardness in the layers increased to 655–680 HV due to lattice expansion, crystallite refinement, and higher dislocation density. However, LSM-treated alloys showed higher corrosion rates and weaker passive films, attributed to increased surface roughness, martensite formation, residual stresses, and microstructural inhomogeneity. Aluminium silicate surface films/residues further compromised passivity. Nevertheless, both LSM-LPBF and LSM-wrought specimens displayed low corrosion current densities (10−4 mA/cm2), true passivity (10−3–10−4 mA/cm2), and high resistance to localised corrosion. After cyclic polarisation, rutile-rich TiO2 surface films with aluminium silicate hydrates were observed. LSM-LPBF specimens showed slightly inferior general corrosion resistance compared to LSM-wrought counterparts, due to pronounced surface texture variations, phase/composition differences, higher microstrains and dislocation density.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光表面熔化对LPBF和锻造Ti-6Al-4V合金微观结构和耐腐蚀性的影响。
summary_zh.method: 对LPBF和锻造Ti-6Al-4V进行激光表面熔化处理，分析微观结构和腐蚀行为。
summary_zh.result: LSM处理提高了显微硬度但降低了耐腐蚀性，LSM-LPBF试样耐蚀性略低于LSM-锻造试样。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微硬度测试和电化学腐蚀实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of laser surface melting (LSM) on microstructure and corrosion resistance of LPBF and wrought Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: LSM was applied to both LPBF and wrought Ti-6Al-4V, followed by microstructural characterization and corrosion testing in simulated body fluid.
summary_en.result: LSM increased microhardness but degraded corrosion resistance, with LSM-LPBF showing slightly inferior general corrosion compared to LSM-wrought.
summary_en.validation: Microhardness measurements and electrochemical corrosion tests.

papers.title: An enhanced characteristic time-based heat input model for simulating laser heating in additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: The Characteristic Time-Based Heat Input (CTI) model is an efficient agglomerated laser approach for simulating a heat source in additive manufacturing, significantly reducing computational costs while maintaining accuracy. In the CTI model, Goldak's moving heat source is applied to laser tracks using a characteristic heating time, based on the ratio of the heat source axis to the scanning speed. However, this characteristic heating time is valid only for material points along the central line of the deposited track, which may lead to applying inaccurate power density distribution at other points within the track. This study enhances the CTI model by reformulating the characteristic heating time through volume averaging the laser exposure time for all points within the semi-elliptical cylinder, achieving more precise temperature predictions while preserving computational efficiency. The improvements of the enhanced CTI (ECTI) model are evaluated through a comparative study with experimental data, the detailed Goldak model, and the original CTI model, focusing on laser-directed energy deposition (DED) of two Ti-6Al-4V components: a thin-wall and a cone. The refined characteristic heating time in the ECTI model demonstrates significant mitigation of temperature history deviation for DED (>7.6% error reduction). The ECTI model shows close agreement with Goldak for residual stress predictions, validated experimentally using the contour method on the cone, and aligns well with experimental measurements of distortion. Additionally, the computational time for the ECTI model is only 23% of that for the Goldak model in the thin-wall geometry and 19.3% in the cone geometry. • Enhanced CTI model was developed by applying an accurate heating time. • ECTI reduces temperature history error to 2.6% (thin-wall) and 7.6% (cone case). • ECTI distortion predictions agree well with experiment and Goldak results. • ECTI cuts runtime to 23% (thin-wall) and 19.3% (cone) of Goldak simulation.

summary_en.motivation: To improve computational efficiency and accuracy of laser heating simulation in additive manufacturing.
summary_en.method: Enhanced characteristic time-based heat input model by volume averaging laser exposure time.
summary_en.result: The enhanced model reduces temperature history error by over 7.6% and cuts computational time to about 20% of the detailed Goldak model.
summary_en.validation: Validated against experimental temperature, residual stress (contour method), and distortion measurements.
